key_insight: The paper shows that conventional FPV can decouple flamelet state selection from the actual local strain-rate field, while an ε-based coupling keeps the flamelet response consistent with the modeled turbulence.
engineering_relevance: For reacting-flow simulations, ε–Z flamelet coupling can improve physical fidelity in high-strain regions and better capture quenching, product persistence, and pressure-dependent flammability limits.
method: 2D RANS simulation of a transonic accelerating reacting mixing layer
Compare one-step kinetics, conventional FPV, and proposed ε–Z flamelet model
Use ε to infer flamelet strain rate S* and transport selected species explicitly
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a numerical comparison against RANS-computed mean strain-rate fields, showing that FPV preferentially samples near-equilibrium states in high-strain regions whereas the ε–Z model maintains strain-rate consistency.
watch_item: The approach adds modeling complexity and depends on reliable ε-to-strain mapping and reactant-availability scaling, which may be sensitive to turbulence-model accuracy and tabulated manifold coverage.
